function: p. 7: MLP-GRU network (Deep LAS) learns bit-wise soft-output LLR values from MMSE-equalized received symbols for MIMO-OFDM detection ahead of a turbo decoder (pp. 4, 7).
system: p. 10: MIMO-OFDM, 4x4 antennas (16 to 256 in Fig. 11b), 4-QAM and 16-QAM, FFT 1024, turbo code rate 1/2; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated.
method: pp. 7-9: Supervised MLP block, then two-sub-block GRU block; trained offline, independently, on LLR targets from the proposed soft-output LAS; MLP with Levenberg-Marquardt, GRU with ADAM.
data_channel: p. 10: Own Matlab simulation, Rayleigh fading 4x4 MIMO-OFDM; target LLRs generated by the proposed soft-output LAS; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurements.
test_conditions: pp. 9-12: Random 80% training, 20% validation split of generated data; BER swept over SNR, FFT length and antenna count, same Rayleigh model; no unseen scenario tested.
baselines: pp. 11-12: Non-learned: conventional ZF- and MMSE-initialized LAS (hard output), optimal sphere decoding (SD). Learned: DetNet, standalone MLP, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU.
metrics: pp. 10-13: BER versus SNR, SNR gain in dB at BER 1e-4 and 1e-5, LLR approximation versus target LLRs, RMSE training loss, per-symbol complexity order.
complexity: p. 13: Big-O per symbol: proposed Deep LAS O(B Nt^2), two-step LAS O(Nt^2); compared with MLD, SD, MMSE, DetNet in Table I.
q1_support: p. 10: "the channel between the transmitter and receiver is assumed to be Rayleigh fading". Custom Rayleigh simulator; p. 13 names "a more realistic 3GPP channel model" only as future work.
q2_support: p. 9: "the randomly selected 80% of the total data points per estimation is used for training while the remaining 20% is used for validation". Held-out part of the same data; no test on a channel, configuration, or scenario unseen in training is stated.
q3_support: p. 11: "BER comparison of the proposed Deep LAS with the other LAS variants, well-known DetNet, and optimal SD algorithm". LAS variants and SD are non-learned, DetNet is an earlier learned detector; p. 12 adds MLP, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU.
q4_support: p. 13: "In total, the computational complexity of the proposed architecture is" O(Nt^2 + B(Nt HK + Nt V^2 + Nt^2 V)), about O(B Nt^2), compared with MLD, SD, MMSE and DetNet in Table I.
q5_support: p. 10: "trained and validated with the data generated using the two-step soft-output LAS". Self-generated Matlab simulation data; no link or DOI to code or data, and no public dataset or measured data.
notes: Included, area 1: learned soft-output MIMO detection by LLR approximation. The proposed two-step soft-output LAS is not learned; only Deep LAS (MLP-GRU) is. The training targets are LLRs from that model-based LAS (pp. 9-10), not exact max-log-MAP LLRs. The input layer has 2Nt neurons (p. 7), so the Fig. 11b runs with other antenna counts imply separate networks; the paper does not state any cross-configuration test.
